algorithm: For each data row, join all cell values with the literal comma character to form one row string.
Sort all row strings ascending lexicographically.
Join the sorted row strings with newline characters and no separately specified trailing newline.
Compute SHA-256 over the exact bytes of the resulting joined string.
Encode the digest as lowercase hexadecimal and store it in row_hash.
edge_cases: Original data-row order does not affect row_hash.
Repeated data rows remain repeated row strings in the hash input.
No trailing newline is added by the specified join operation.
The header does not participate in row_hash.

formatting.value: One newline character between adjacent sorted row strings.

input_schema.value: All parsed CSV data rows, excluding the header.
Use each parsed cell value as its string value.

integration.value: Replaces only the row_hash digest algorithm and length; active snapshot row_count, column_count, column statistics, and header-order requirements remain unchanged.

invariants: Identical multisets of parsed data rows produce identical row_hash values.
row_hash uses SHA-256 rather than MD5.
No snapshot output field other than row_hash is changed by this migration.
ordering: Row strings are sorted ascending lexicographically before joining and hashing.
All existing snapshot output-field and sorting rules remain unchanged.

output_schema.value: Exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding the SHA-256 digest of the sorted row-content string.

preconditions: The input CSV has been parsed and the header excluded from data_rows.
spec.summary: Compute snapshot row_hash as lowercase SHA-256 over the same lexicographically sorted, comma-joined data-row content previously used for snapshot hashing.

algorithm: Read value as a literal string; do not parse or evaluate it as an expression.
Append a new header column whose name is the as field.
For every current data row, append the tag value produced by the literal-assignment requirement.
edge_cases: A dataset with zero data rows still receives the appended header column.
The tag operation does not remove or modify existing columns.

examples.name: production environment tag
examples.notes: Every data row receives production in the appended column.
examples.output: A final column named env is appended.

input_schema.value: String constant to stamp on every data row.
String name of the new column to append.

integration.value: Runs as one operation in the ordered transform recipe chain.
Use req-r015-003 for every appended data cell.
Use req-r015-004 before modifying the dataset.

invariants: Exactly one new column is appended on success.
Existing rows and cells retain their relative order and values.
ordering: Preserve all existing column order and append the as column last.

output_schema.value: All existing columns in their existing order followed by one new column named by as.
One output row per current input row, with the tag result appended.

preconditions: The as field is present and non-empty.
spec.summary: Provide a tag transform that accepts a literal string and appends a named column to the current dataset.

algorithm: Treat value as a literal string rather than a derive expression.
For each data row, append the exact value string.
Do not vary or recompute the value between rows.
edge_cases: An empty value string is stamped as an empty cell on every row.
No expression operators, functions, or column references are evaluated within value.
With zero data rows, no data cells are produced.

examples.name: literal tag assignment
examples.output: Every row's env cell is exactly "production".

formulas.value: value for every data-row index i

input_schema.value: The tag operation's string value field.

integration.value: The result is written to the last column appended by req-r015-002.
Unlike derive, tag performs no expression evaluation.

invariants: Every output row receives the same exact configured string.
Tag assignment is independent of all existing row values.
ordering: Process and emit rows in their current order.

output_schema.value: The exact configured value string, copied without expression evaluation or numeric conversion.

preconditions: The tag operation passed as-field validation.
spec.summary: Copy the configured tag value literally and identically into the appended cell of every data row.

algorithm: Before appending the header or modifying rows, determine whether as is missing or equals the empty string.
If as is missing or empty, return the exact error text and do not execute the tag assignment.
Otherwise continue with the tag operation.
edge_cases: An explicitly empty as value is treated the same as an omitted as field.

errors.condition: The tag as field is missing or empty.

input_schema.value: Required non-empty string naming the appended tag column.

invariants: A missing or empty as field never produces a tagged dataset.
The returned error text is exactly ERROR: invalid recipe: missing 'as' field.
notes: The instruction specifies the returned error text but does not specify an exit code or stdout/stderr channel.
ordering: Validate as before changing the dataset.
spec.summary: Reject a tag operation whose as field is missing or empty with the exact specified error text.
